topics.title: Source positioning
notes: Observed: TEKLA positions itself as a considered, materials-first home-textile brand built to correct what it calls thin, undifferentiated bedding — "Tekla was built around uniting form and function" and was "created as an antidote to the bedding available at the time" (EV-001).

topics.title: Core causal model
notes: Inferred: a restrained visual system (near-black wordmark on a warm off-white field, EV-003) plus centered, negative-space-heavy product photography (EV-102) plus explicit longevity language (EV-001) work together to argue that the product is worth a premium because it will last, not because it is decorated (EV-001, EV-102).

topics.title: Contrasting qualities that stay together
notes: Observed: a domestic, lived-in warmth (wood, kilim rugs, cherry blossom branches, EV-104) is kept next to an almost clinical product-detail register (macro label crops, flat-lay stacks, EV-105, EV-106) — softness in the world, precision in the proof.

topics.title: What this analysis does not claim
notes: This package makes no claim about TEKLA's internal design system files, its full logo guideline set, unpublished pricing, or any category TEKLA has not itself entered. No target brand, transfer, or fictional name is present anywhere in this file.

topics.title: Source-tier and channel coverage
notes: Observed: primary evidence is the live teklafabrics.com homepage and About page copy (EV-001, EV-002) plus a direct capture of the shipped CSS/meta bundle (EV-003); secondary evidence is three press features (Wallpaper*, Scandinavia Standard, Forbes; EV-004, EV-005, EV-006) used only for corroborating, attributed description.

topics.title: Era, region, product-line, campaign, and collaborator strata
notes: Observed: all evidence is dated 2020–2026 and reflects the current global masterbrand; no collaborator or guest-collection material was collected, matching the brief's exclusions.

topics.title: Visual corpus and contact sheets
notes: Observed: 10 direct local visuals span identity (EV-101), key visual (EV-102), photography (EV-103, EV-110), brand mood (EV-104), product representation (EV-105, EV-106, EV-109), and product-native language (EV-107, EV-108); contact sheets are in `contact-sheets/`.

topics.title: Biases, contradictions, and gaps
notes: Observed gap: the rapid window did not isolate a clean, standalone wordmark lockup file — the favicon/app-icon mark (EV-101) is the only official standalone identity asset captured, while the fuller "TEKLA" wordmark is only observed in situ on the storefront (EV-104) and on woven product labels (EV-105, EV-106, EV-108). This is recorded as an unresolved gap, not inferred into a fabricated logo file.

topics.title: Category definition
notes: Observed: TEKLA frames its category as everyday home textiles — bedding, bath, sleepwear, and home accessories — rather than luxury linen or interior design (EV-001, EV-002).

topics.title: Audience identity, situation, and anxieties
notes: Inferred: the brand addresses a buyer who already owns adequate bedding but is dissatisfied with its quality or design, since the founding narrative is explicitly framed against "the bedding available at the time" (EV-001, EV-005).

topics.title: Tension or enemy
notes: Observed: the named tension is rapid trend cycles and disposable home goods — TEKLA states it "rejects rapid trend cycles, designing for longevity" and that growth should not mean encouraging existing customers "to consume more than they need" (EV-001).

topics.title: Functional, emotional, and social promise
notes: Observed: functionally, "pieces are designed to be lived in and made to last"; emotionally, the promise is calm domestic comfort signalled by soft-focus lifestyle imagery (EV-001, EV-103).

topics.title: Reasons to believe
notes: Observed: B Corp certification, named production-partner collaboration, and "uncompromising quality" language are offered as proof points for the durability claim (EV-001).

topics.title: Competitive and cultural posture
notes: Inferred: press coverage repeatedly places TEKLA against European modernist reference points — Alvar Aalto, Mies van der Rohe, Axel Vervoordt — positioning it culturally nearer architecture and design culture than fashion or bedding retail (EV-004, EV-006).

topics.title: Portfolio, endorsement, and authorship logic
notes: Observed: all captured evidence is first-party masterbrand material; no sub-brand, endorsement, or collaborator authorship structure was found within the rapid window (EV-001, EV-002).

topics.title: Lexicon and semantic territories
notes: Observed: recurring vocabulary centers on "quality," "longevity," "lived in," "made to last," and "form and function" rather than luxury, trend, or fashion vocabulary (EV-001).

topics.title: Syntax, rhetoric, cadence, and emotional temperature
notes: Observed: sentences are short, declarative, and value-led ("We make a case for quality, design and longevity across our entire value chain"), avoiding superlatives (EV-001).

topics.title: Message hierarchy
notes: Observed: mission and values statements lead the About page; product and collection promotion follows on the homepage (EV-001, EV-002).

topics.title: Naming behavior
notes: Observed: product names combine a material/construction term with a place or pattern name, e.g. "Core Down Duvet," "Percale Pillow Sham Douglas Checks," "Terry Classic Bathrobe Marseille" (EV-106, EV-107, EV-109).

topics.title: Campaign, product, UI, transactional, support, and error modulation
notes: Observed: homepage promotional copy stays close to plain description ("Discover sleepwear in refreshed colours," "Fresh cotton bedding") rather than campaign-style copywriting (EV-002).

topics.title: Verbal exceptions and proprietary language
notes: Observed: "B Corp" and value-chain/ESG language are used precisely rather than loosely, consistent with a certification claim (EV-001).

topics.title: Verbal brand hierarchy
notes: > Synthesize only evidence already collected in strategy and verbal sections. Use `gap` when a level is not explicitly supported; do not extend research to fill it.

topics.title: Mark behavior
notes: Observed: the favicon/app-icon mark (EV-101) is a dark mark on a light field, matching the site's `#181818` theme-color and mask-icon color (EV-003); the fuller "TEKLA" wordmark is set in a bold, tightly tracked, geometric all-caps sans-serif wherever observed in situ — storefront signage (EV-104) and woven product labels (EV-105, EV-106, EV-108).

topics.title: Typography roles and relationships
notes: Observed: the live site self-hosts one family, Unica77, in Regular (400), Light (300), and Light Italic weights, applied via `--font-unica77` with a `ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif` fallback stack (EV-003).

topics.title: Color roles, value structure, concentrated accent use, and image relationship
notes: Observed: the page canvas resolves to `#F6F6F6` and the persistent ink/active/border color resolves to `#181818` across the shipped CSS, the `theme-color` meta tag, and the `safari-pinned-tab` mask-icon color — three independent confirmations of the same identity pair (EV-003).

topics.title: Spacing, grid, containers, density, and responsive behavior
notes: Observed gap: layout/grid metrics were not measured within the rapid window; recorded as an unresolved gap rather than invented.

topics.title: Shape, surface, depth, icon, illustration, and motion primitives
notes: Observed: no illustration or iconography system beyond the single monogram mark was found; product labels use plain rectangular woven tags (EV-105, EV-106, EV-108).

topics.title: Owned-digital implementation versus cross-channel invariants
notes: Observed: the `#181818` / `#F6F6F6` pairing and the black wordmark recur identically across the owned site chrome (EV-003) and the physical storefront/product labels (EV-104, EV-105, EV-106, EV-108), so it is treated as a cross-channel invariant rather than a digital-only convention.

topics.title: Typography, color, form, layout, and material relationship
notes: Observed: the same `#181818` ink recurs as digital text/UI color (EV-003), physical wordmark ink (EV-104), and woven label ink (EV-105, EV-106, EV-108), tying digital and physical identity together through one consistent dark value rather than through a shared typeface file, since the storefront/label wordmark weight was not confirmed to be Unica77 itself.

topics.title: UI, content-template, imagery, and motion translation
notes: Observed gap: UI component and motion translation were not measured within the rapid window.

topics.title: Masterbrand versus campaign/collaborator/season authorship
notes: Observed: every captured surface (site, store, product label) carries the same masterbrand wordmark with no collaborator or seasonal sub-mark observed (EV-101, EV-104, EV-105, EV-106, EV-108).

topics.title: Invariants, variables, and prohibited generalizations
notes: Invariant: the `#181818` / `#F6F6F6` identity pair and centered, negative-space product framing. Variable: photographic palette by product line and season. Prohibited generalization: treating any single product's campaign color (e.g. sage duvet, cornflower robe) as a masterbrand identity color.

topics.title: Cultural and emotional register
notes: Observed: calm, undecorated, materially confident — closer to architecture/design editorial than fashion campaign register (EV-004, EV-006).

topics.title: Reality versus fiction
notes: Observed: settings are real, existing spaces (the actual Egmont Building flagship, plain studio interiors) rather than constructed fictional sets (EV-104).

topics.title: Settings, environments, material imagination, and sensory register
notes: Observed: natural materials recur — wood counters, concrete floors, cherry-blossom branches, kilim rugs, birch bentwood furniture (EV-104, EV-110).

topics.title: Human role and social distance
notes: Observed: when people appear, they are shown at a private, undemonstrative distance (seated, gaze averted, or a plain frontal fit portrait) rather than in an active social scene (EV-103, EV-109).

topics.title: Production causes that create the mood
notes: Inferred: soft, low-contrast lighting and restrained color grading (EV-103, EV-110) combined with real, un-styled-looking rooms (EV-104) are the two production choices that build the "serene" register press coverage names (EV-004).

topics.title: Subjects, casting, gaze, gesture, wardrobe, and styling
notes: Observed: single models in TEKLA sleepwear/robes, gaze often averted or neutral rather than smiling at camera (EV-103, EV-109).

topics.title: Location, set, props, and environmental realism
notes: Observed: real domestic-scale interiors and one vintage furniture prop (birch bentwood trolley) rather than an abstract studio cyclorama in every shot (EV-104, EV-110).

topics.title: Framing, camera distance/height, perspective, and lens character
notes: Observed: a consistent alternation between frontal eye-level portraits/product shots (EV-102, EV-109) and top-down or macro detail crops (EV-105, EV-106, EV-107, EV-108).

topics.title: Light, exposure, reflection, shadow, palette, and time
notes: Observed: two lighting registers are used — soft even studio light for product/detail images, and low-key directional window light for lifestyle portraiture (EV-103 vs. EV-106).

topics.title: Texture, imperfection, retouching, compositing, and typography in image
notes: Observed: fabric creasing and natural texture are kept visible rather than fully smoothed in detail crops (EV-106, EV-107).

topics.title: Motion, cuts, transitions, loops, and sound
notes: Observed gap: no motion/video asset was captured within the rapid window.

topics.title: Channel variants and exceptions
notes: Observed: press-sourced imagery (store opening) uses documentary framing rather than the brand's own controlled studio setup (EV-104).

topics.title: Physical-product photography and neutral views
notes: Observed: duvets and towels are shown both as full, centered hero objects (EV-102) and as isolated flat-lay/macro crops (EV-105, EV-106).

topics.title: Digital-product mockups, screenshots, and screen recordings
notes: Not applicable: TEKLA's product line is physical home textiles; no digital-product surface was found (product_mode: physical).

topics.title: Family views, detail, scale, and material fidelity
notes: Observed: the towel stack image shows one product across its full size range with the same label repeated at every size (EV-105).

topics.title: Product in use and human relationship
notes: Observed: the bathrobe is shown worn, front-on, hands in pockets, to demonstrate fit and drape (EV-109).

topics.title: Operation, performance, and factual demonstration
notes: Observed: care/size information is shown directly on the woven label within the product photography itself rather than as separate overlay text (EV-106).

topics.title: Packaging, onboarding, care, support, failure, and recovery representation
notes: Observed gap: packaging, onboarding, and support imagery were not captured within the rapid window.

topics.title: Camera, device frame, capture, retouching, compositing, and channel limits
notes: Observed: all captured product imagery is straight photography with light retouching; no 3D render or device-frame mockup was found (EV-105, EV-106, EV-107, EV-108, EV-109).

topics.title: Shared product model: category archetype or mental model
notes: Observed: TEKLA's products read as functional textile staples (a duvet, a towel, a robe, a slipper) rather than as decorative objects — construction and material are foregrounded over ornament (EV-106, EV-107, EV-108).

topics.title: Shared hierarchy, structure, boundaries, controls, states, and feedback
notes: Not applicable in a UI sense; the physical equivalent is the woven label, which consistently carries brand name, then product line, then size/spec, in that order (EV-106).

topics.title: Physical branch: silhouette, proportion, geometry, CMF, seams, joints, and movement
notes: Observed: channel-quilted duvet construction, ribbed piping on sleepwear and robes, and pile shearling on slippers are all shown as legible, close-up construction details rather than hidden (EV-106, EV-107, EV-108).

topics.title: Physical branch: care, storage, repair, wear, and failure
notes: Observed gap: care, storage, and repair imagery were not captured within the rapid window.

topics.title: Product-family invariants and controlled variants
notes: Observed: the rectangular woven label with all-caps "TEKLA" wordmark is the one constant across every product category captured (bedding, bath, slippers) (EV-105, EV-106, EV-108).

topics.title: Hybrid branch: physical control, digital state, service, and feedback continuity
notes: Not applicable: no hybrid physical/digital product was found within scope.

topics.title: Product truth versus photography, mockup, screenshot, and campaign construction
notes: Observed: detail crops (EV-106, EV-107, EV-108) show real, unretouched construction rather than an idealized render, which the analysis treats as the more reliable product-truth evidence relative to the styled key visual (EV-102).

topics.title: Grid, anchoring, grouping, density, and whitespace
notes: Observed: centered anchoring with wide negative space recurs across the key visual, the storefront window, and the styled still life (EV-102, EV-104, EV-110).

topics.title: Scale, crop, overlap, repetition, and interruption
notes: Observed: product-detail images use tight, non-overlapping macro crops (EV-106, EV-107), while world/lifestyle images allow layered depth and prop overlap (EV-110).

topics.title: Relationships among type, image, object, product, and space
notes: Observed: type appears physically in-frame (signage, labels) rather than as a graphic overlay layer in every captured image (EV-104, EV-105, EV-106, EV-108).

notes: Observed gap: responsive/format adaptation was not measured within the rapid window.

notes: Observed: the homepage groups by category (Bed, Bath, Clothing, Home, Gift Shop) with collection and bestseller cross-links, and offers a 10%-off newsletter incentive (EV-002).

topics.title: Defaults, permissions, guidance, tempo, and feedback
notes: Observed: the site exposes size guides, care information, and a store locator as standing utility links alongside product navigation (EV-002).

topics.title: Error, recovery, and service escalation
notes: Observed gap: error and recovery states were not captured within the rapid window.

topics.title: Product ceremony, onboarding, use, care, repair, and post-purchase
notes: Observed: care/spec information is delivered on the physical woven label itself (EV-106) rather than only through a digital care guide, consistent with the brand's "designed to be lived in" language (EV-001).

grammar_rules.name: Center one product in a plain field
grammar_rules.input_condition: A single hero product (a made bed, a folded product family) needs to read as the brand's default visual statement.
grammar_rules.transformation: Place the product frontally at the center of the frame against one plain, lightly textured surface, leaving roughly half or more of the frame as surrounding negative space.
grammar_rules.intended_effect: The product reads as calm and considered rather than styled or crowded, before any lifestyle context is added.
grammar_rules.alternative_explanation: Minimal styling could simply reflect e-commerce photography convenience rather than a deliberate key-visual rule.
grammar_rules.exception_and_scope: Applies to the current global masterbrand's owned-web hero imagery and flagship storefront window only.
grammar_rules.protected_source_expression: Do not copy TEKLA's own photographs; reproduce only the compositional relationship.
grammar_rules.acceptance_test: The primary subject is centered with visibly dominant plain surrounding field.
grammar_rules.rejection_test: Multiple competing subjects or heavy prop styling fill the frame edge to edge.

grammar_rules.name: Separate label proof from mood photography
grammar_rules.input_condition: A product's material/construction truth and a lifestyle emotional register both need representation.
grammar_rules.transformation: Give each image exactly one job — either a clinical macro/flat-lay crop showing label, weave, and construction, or a soft, low-key lifestyle portrait — and never merge the two in one frame.
grammar_rules.intended_effect: Construction claims stay verifiable and uncluttered while mood imagery stays emotionally legible, without either undercutting the other.
grammar_rules.alternative_explanation: The separation could be an artifact of using different photographers or shoot days rather than an intentional rule.
grammar_rules.exception_and_scope: Applies to captured owned-web product and lifestyle imagery only; campaign video was not assessed.
grammar_rules.protected_source_expression: Do not copy TEKLA's specific label typesetting or exact crop; reuse only the separation-of-jobs principle.
grammar_rules.acceptance_test: Every sampled image can be labeled as either a detail/proof shot or a mood shot, not both.
grammar_rules.rejection_test: One image simultaneously shows legible label/construction detail and an active lifestyle scene.

grammar_rules.name: Repeat the same woven label across every category
grammar_rules.input_condition: A new product category (bedding, bath, slippers) needs a brand-recognition anchor without adding a new graphic system per category.
grammar_rules.transformation: Apply one rectangular woven label, black all-caps TEKLA wordmark on a light ribbon, with product line and size/spec beneath it, at a consistent seam or vamp location.
grammar_rules.intended_effect: Any product photograph, regardless of category, can be identified as TEKLA from the same small physical detail.
grammar_rules.alternative_explanation: Consistent labeling may simply follow generic textile-industry labeling convention rather than a deliberate brand rule.
grammar_rules.exception_and_scope: Confirmed for bedding, bath, and slipper categories only; not confirmed for candles or other home-decor items.
grammar_rules.protected_source_expression: Do not copy the exact label artwork; reuse only the label-hierarchy and placement principle.
grammar_rules.acceptance_test: The same label hierarchy (wordmark, then line, then spec) appears in a newly sampled product image.
grammar_rules.rejection_test: A sampled product category shows no label or a differently ordered hierarchy.

grammar_rules.name: Carry one dark identity value across every surface
grammar_rules.input_condition: The same brand needs to be recognizable across a digital screen, a physical storefront, and a sewn product label, none of which share a rendering technology.
grammar_rules.transformation: Apply the same near-black value (#181818) as text/mark ink on every surface — CSS text and borders on the site, painted or printed signage in the store, and printed wordmark ink on woven labels — against a consistently light ground.
grammar_rules.intended_effect: Identity recognition survives a change of material and medium without requiring a shared font file or asset format.
grammar_rules.alternative_explanation: Near-black ink on a light ground is also just a common, generic print/UI default, not necessarily an intentional brand rule.
grammar_rules.exception_and_scope: Confirmed for owned web, the Copenhagen flagship, and sampled woven labels; not confirmed for packaging or other unsampled physical media.
grammar_rules.protected_source_expression: Do not copy TEKLA's exact CSS or label artwork; reuse only the cross-medium dark-ink-on-light-ground principle.
grammar_rules.acceptance_test: A newly sampled TEKLA surface uses a near-black mark on a light ground.
grammar_rules.rejection_test: A newly sampled TEKLA surface uses a materially different identity color pairing.
